headless.priming: Statistics revision 3 (#1536): before block 0, one unscored run per arm per workload x topology, arm A (slot -2, the declared topology order) then arm B (slot -1, reversed), the same alternation as the scored slots, which count from 0. Each is its own process like any run, recorded in runs.jsonl with primed: true and block null, and listed in the session record (priming) and the session-end record (primedRuns). They are never analysed and are outside the failed-run rule; a missing or failed priming run leaves the set not judged (statistics.revisionNote). Priming runs are never retried: a session with a failed priming run ends after the priming pass, before block 0, and its session-end record says why (stopped). The report adds a descriptive block-0 check (block 0's B/A - 1 against the RMS of the later blocks') so a rev-3 A/A shows whether the cold start is gone. The browser runner has no priming pass: it measures one arm (no A/B, so no comparison a cold arm could bias), its seeding run already starts the same API binary serving the same dist before the first measured run, and its cell order rotates every round. Its baseline data shows no cold first run to remove: its slow runs are not confined to the session's first run but span the early rounds (rounds 0-2 at most positions, and the first run of rounds 0-3), which one unscored run would not absorb.

accounting.declared: Browser accounting revision 2 (#1557), declared before any run under it; it replaces revision 1's fail-closed refusal. Simulated work is the frames the kernel actually completed, read from the bench's pacing timeline (User Timing measures: one per task slice with the frames admitted, attempted and completed and the debt left; one per discarded remainder), never interval count x selected rate. The window opens and closes between tasks, so every slice lies wholly inside or outside it (a straddling slice refuses the run); frames admitted before the window and completed inside it count, and the debt open at each boundary is recorded. Every entry of the measured pacing epoch is conserved from its first admission (admitted = attempted + discarded + outstanding); a missing, extra or reordered entry, a second epoch in the window, a slice outside an observed timer task, or no timeline at all (an arm built before the timeline existed) refuses the run, which is recorded as failed with its numbers. A lost entry is visible only through a later entry of its epoch, so the window must be closed by one: the epoch continues past the window end (the run waits briefly for it), or it ends inside the window with its discard; otherwise the run refuses. The window loop ends early, and the window is accounted, as soon as an interaction step adds no completed frames (no timeline, a mission end, a fault or a pause). Throughput is completed simulated seconds per wall second, reported beside the selected rate (achieved / selected). Simulation cost (slice durations) is reported separately from continuation cost (the yield gap from one slice's end to the next slice of its batch, and the task tail: the rest of the slice's timer task through the microtask queued after it). A yield gap contains the earlier task's tail, so gaps and tails are not added; long tasks, Long Animation Frames, rAF and Event Timing stay separately attributed. The window runs until it holds windowSimSeconds of completed simulation. The run record keeps the window instants and the epoch's completed frames before the window (the warm-up's executed work). Browser levels are descriptive only, and this revision admits no browser budget verdict: #1542 first requires a counterbalanced browser protocol revision (the run order restored here still starts every round with a 1x cell and ends it with a 64x cell), and then a quiet-host browser A/A under that revision. Revision 1 refusal records and v1 interval-inferred records keep their original identities and are reported NOT_QUALIFIED. Headless statistics revision 3 is unchanged.

interaction.pairs: two presses 1 s apart (brighten, then dim back), a pair every 6 s of wall time in the window

statistics.revisionNote: Revision 3 (#1536), declared before any run under it. A headless session now opens with a priming pass before block 0 (headless.priming): one unscored run per arm per workload x topology, arm A then arm B. Priming runs are recorded with primed: true and never analysed (no test, interval, comparison 5 or absolute level uses them), and they are outside the failed-run rule. A headless run set is judged only when it comes from exactly one session (blocks are numbered from 0 in each session) and that session recorded the declared priming pass with every priming run present and passed; otherwise it is not judged. Reason: every session opened on arm A, and in the revision-2 A/A the session's first three processes were cold, about 65 s in all: p50 +36.0% (W1 single), +38.8% (W1 dual) and +68.7% (W2 single) against the median of the same arm and cell. Every later first run of a cell, on either arm, was within -2.1% to +2.2%. In an A/B, A is the base, so B/A - 1 was biased toward B faster, which hides slowdowns. Nothing else in this block changed: the test, R, Holm over the same 40 comparisons, alpha and the failed-run rule are as in revision 2. Revision 2 (#1519 review) replaced revision 1's two-sided bootstrap p (0 far too often under the null: a 21% family fail rate over 150 ABBA-preserving relabellings of the real A/A data) with the within-block permutation test. Recorded verdicts stand under their own revisions: the revision-1 A/A FAILED, the revision-2 A/A PASSED (#1510, 6 Oct). Neither carries over: revision 3 applies only to runs taken after it was committed, and it needs its own quiet-host A/A before any A/B budget claim.
statistics.testDefinition: Statistic: |ln(median B / median A)| over all of a cell's runs, the two-sided form of B/A - 1 of the arm medians. Under the null the runs of each ABBA block are exchangeable between arms: each block's labels are re-dealt keeping two A and two B, 6 labellings per block, independently across blocks. R labellings are drawn with the seeded generator; p = (c + 1) / (R + 1), c the drawn labellings whose statistic is at or above the observed one (1e-12 tolerance). Exact enumeration (p = count / labellings, observed included) is used only when the labellings number no more than R.
statistics.smallestAttainableP: max(1 / (R + 1), 2 / 6^blocks) = 1 / 20000 = 5e-5 for 10 blocks, below alpha / m = 0.05 / 40 = 1.25e-3. An arm flip per block alone (2^10 = 1024 labellings) could not go below 2 / 1024 = 2e-3 and is not used.
statistics.multiplicity: Holm step-down over the family of aaMeasures x cells (40), family-wise alpha aaFamilyAlpha; a comparison is significant when its Holm-adjusted p <= alpha. A family whose smallest attainable p is not below alpha / m is refused, not passed.
statistics.intervals: 95% intervals are descriptive bootstrap intervals, not the test: resampling runs with replacement within each (block, arm) group, k - 1 draws from a group of k (McCarthy and Snowden), exact enumeration when the distinct resamples number no more than iterations, otherwise iterations draws; nearest-rank 2.5% and 97.5% of the replicates. Absolute levels resample a cell's runs as one group (n - 1 draws).
statistics.percentiles: nearest rank, ceil(p / 100 x n), for per-run frame percentiles, interval ends and the interaction p50
statistics.failedRun: A block in which any run of a cell failed is excluded whole from that cell's analysis (both arms) and the exclusion is reported; failed runs are kept in the record.
statistics.notApplicable: Worker backlog (D10 12.2): not applicable before I3; there is no worker before then.

baseline.declared: After both pilots and before any baseline run. The browser windows (60 s at 1x, 2400 s at 64x) and the 15 s warm-up are kept as declared before the pilot.
baseline.headlessReason: the pilot's half-widths (1.7 to 75.04 pp at 4 runs per arm) plan more than the cap for every cell, so N = 20 runs per arm (10 ABBA blocks), the cap
baseline.browserReason: the pilot plans the cap of 10 for seven of the eight cells (4 for view-off-svs-off at 64x); every round runs every cell, so 10 rounds

quietHost.revision: Tightened after the headless pilot and before any baseline run: the pilot's criterion (3 s, 25%, 60 s) admitted runs that other work on the shared host slowed by up to 30%. A run that starts after the wait without meeting it is still run, flagged and kept.
